title: Causal Forcing: Autoregressive Diffusion Distillation Done Right for High-Quality Real-Time Interactive Video Generation
claim: The leading distillation approach into causal students produces degraded, less dynamic, less faithful outputs than its bidirectional counterpart, revealing a gap to close.
layout: 2 rows of frames left-to-right, with bar chart on right
description: The figure has two parts. On the left are two rows of video frames from the same prompt, a scientist in a white lab coat in a futuristic glass lab at night. The top row is labeled Standard DMD and shows a coherent scene where the scientist turns and moves naturally. The bottom row is labeled Self Forcing and shows frames that gradually lose quality. The scientist stays mostly static and blurs or fades in the later frames. Ellipses between the frames mark the passage of time. On the right is a bar chart with a y-axis from 40 to 70. It compares Standard DMD (blue) and Self Forcing (purple) on Dynamic Degree and Instruction Following, and Standard DMD scores higher on both. The eye goes first to the vivid frames, then to the bars.
caption: Limitations of existing methods. While distilling from the same bidirectional base model, SOTA autoregressive diffusion distillation methods like Self-Forcing still lag significantly behind standard DMD, which distills a bidirectional student.
abstract: To achieve real-time interactive video generation, current methods distill pretrained bidirectional video diffusion models into few-step autoregressive (AR) models, facing an architectural gap when full attention is replaced by causal attention. However, existing approaches do not bridge this gap theoretically. They initialize the AR student via ODE distillation, which requires frame-level injectivity, where each noisy frame must map to a unique clean frame under the PF-ODE of an AR teacher. Distilling an AR student from a bidirectional teacher violates this condition, preventing recovery of the teacher's flow map and instead inducing a conditional-expectation solution, which degrades performance. To address this issue, we propose Causal Forcing, which uses an autoregressive teacher for ODE initialization to bridge the architectural gap, and then applies the same DMD procedure as in Self Forcing. Empirical results show that our method outperforms all baselines across all metrics, surpassing the SOTA Self Forcing by 19.3\% in Dynamic Degree, 8.7\% in VisionReward, and 16.7\% in Instruction Following.
